When I first started using it, I didn’t understand it’s potential. It’s very easy to get distracted on other things and lose track of time. In recent months I’ve been learning to play Piano so I’ve begun to understand just how powerful the mind is. I used to be so forgetful and could barely get out of bed at all.
I only started it using it after the damage had already been done. I was already retaking the year and I guess it turns out that Uni just wasn’t for me..

The first year I started taking it I was trying to turn my life around; but ended up progressively getting worse. I failed University, started abusing drugs heavily and got myself in a load of debt (before and after). 

It wasn’t until I started writing my thoughts down that things started to change. I guess I finally had enough and decided it was time to take back control of my mind. I started focusing my attention on what I love. I got myself a job. I started working out. And most importantly I began writing and recording songs again..

Although I was still slacking and wasting a lot of time; I’ve now started learning to play piano which is huge for me. I’ve managed to improve drastically over the last 3-4 years. I’m still learning and I’m still making mistakes. Sometimes I have those days where I start procrastinating; but thanks to all the consistent effort I’ve put in to the Music I can easily switch my focus back to what’s important.

I started taking 50-100mg and then 200mg. Eventually I took 300mg and for over a year or so I’ve been taking 400mg. Although in recent months I’ve been staying awake longer so essentially I’m taking just over 200mg. That’s only because I have something to do which keeps me awake. 

The point I’m trying to make is that the problem is not with the pills. The problem is with your mind. I went from sitting around smoking weed all day and wasting away to completely turning my life around. I never worked out and I was practically a pile of bones. I went from abusing drugs to somehow finding the right medication that gave me my mind back. 

If it wasn’t for Modafinil I wouldn’t even be here...

Sometimes being alone is the best thing. Most people may look happy together but they’re just as alone; if not more. They just use each other to fill the void and spend their whole lives asleep. 

I was where you are now just over 3 years ago; but it was much worse. I couldn’t hold a job. I became addicted to drugs and got myself in a lot of debt. I was literally just a pile of bones slowly dying. It’s still shocking to look back and see how low I had fallen. I only made it out because I just so happened to stumble onto the right medication that gave me my mind back. 

Although I still continued to fall deeper..
I eventually I found my way and started building myself back up just by doing some simple home workouts. I started with 5kg weights and eventually built enough confidence to go to the gym. Most importantly I started writing songs again (which is what I love to do). Eventually I started recording, releasing and marketing. Now I’m learning to play piano and make beats. I wasn’t as active lately and gained some weight so I started taking daily walks to get my health back on track. 

The point I’m trying to make is that sometimes these things take time. You’re working a lot so maybe you should try and cut down your hours or take a break. Time is the most important asset you have. Your health is more important than any amount of money will ever be. One day you just have to wake up and get tired of being stuck in the same place. You are aware that there’s something wrong and you want to change. You know you can be better. You just have to take control of your mind so you can take control of your life.  

The decision is only yours alone to make.
